subject: Air-gapped acceptance criteria and roll-forward plan for Gravitas private deployment
messages:
From: Rachel Wong <rachel.wong@gravitashealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, ops_team@gravitashealth.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Air-gapped update window & validation expectations

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We are moving toward an on-site maintenance window for the sealed cluster and need Redwood's formal acceptance criteria for an air-gapped image update. Specifically:

- What must be present in the signed image manifest and how do we verify signatures offline?
- Which post-install validation checks do you expect the customer to run during the maintenance window to sign off on a successful update?
- If a rollback is required, what is the recommended roll-forward/roll-back timeline and who needs to be looped in?

We have an internal change freeze on 2026-11-22 and would like to schedule the image handoff, validation, and signoff earlier that week. Please also include any artifacts you will attach so our security team can pre-approve them.

Attachments: none in this initial note.

Thanks,
Rachel Wong
Head of Infrastructure, Gravitas Health Systems
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T11:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped update window & validation expectations

Rachel — thanks, quick reply with a consolidated validation matrix and a pragmatic roll-forward plan. Attaching the checklist and the signed manifest.

Summary (high level):
- Signed image manifest: must include image SHA256, build timestamp, builder ID, and a detached signature (.sig) from Redwood's release key. We also include the public signing certificate (external-signer-certificate.pem) so you can validate signatures offline with openssl.
- Offline verification steps (customer):
  1) Verify digest: sha256sum <image>.tar.gz and compare to manifest.sha256
  2) Verify signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify external-signer-certificate.pem -signature signed-image-manifest.json.sig signed-image-manifest.json
  3) Validate manifest fields: expected model hash, allowed quantization flags, and recommended runtime kernel profile (included in manifest).
- Post-install acceptance gates (to be executed in order):
  A) Node health checks: all nodes reach Running state, kubelet certs present, KV cache warm for baseline prompt sets (scripts included).
  B) Functional smoke: 10 deterministic prompt rounds (provided prompt set) with token-consistent responses (sufficient for regression detection).
  C) Latency spot checks: 95th percentile below agreed SLO for the seed workload (scripts generate load locally).
  D) Audit log verification: last-token events recorded and signed by the runtime (local logs present and checksummed).

Roll-forward & rollback plan (brief):
- If acceptance gates A–D pass within the maintenance window (target 90 minutes), signoff: customer indicates PASS and Redwood finalizes post-deploy verification report.
- If a non-blocking regression is observed (e.g., minor latency drift), proceed with roll-forward: increase canary traffic to 30% for 60 minutes with close monitoring; if stable, complete rollout.
- If a blocking failure occurs (model mismatch, severe functional regression), immediate rollback to previous signed image (image tag + pre-generated signed manifest included). Rollback action target: 30–45 minutes for restore + 30 minutes to re-run gates.

Attached: offline-artifacts-checklist.csv, signed-image-manifest.json.sig, rollforward-playbook.pdf, external-signer-certificate.pem

Notes & caveats:
- The attached playbook includes step-by-step CLI commands for offline environments; where networked time sources aren't available, use hardware clock comparisons included in the checklist.
- We recommend a single point-of-contact on site for Redwood to speak to during the window (ops_team@gravitashealth.com recommended).

Happy to walk through this in a call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Adding a few technical acceptance gates and a small request from the infra team. Quoting Stephanie below for context.

> Post-install acceptance gates (to be executed in order):
> A) Node health checks...
> B) Functional smoke...

Additional infra-level checks (must be automated where possible):
- Crypto key availability: confirm KMS proxy (if used) is reachable from the sealed environment or that keys are pre-wrapped and present. We will include a key-wrapping example in the checklist.
- KV cache sanity: verify cache warm-up using the provided warmup script; failure if < 70% of expected entries populate within 10 minutes.
- Disk signature validation: verify that the downloaded image file has an accompanying signed manifest and that the signer chain resolves to the provided external-signer-certificate.pem; explicit step included to validate certificate fingerprint.
- Emergency fallback route: in addition to restore from previous image, ensure config snapshot of traffic routing rules is taken before the window. This allows rapid rollback of routing in case the runtime is healthy but network policies prevent traffic flow.

Operational ask for Gravitas: please confirm on-site POC and whether the on-prem host has physical media access (USB) or only network-isolated transfer (we need to know media transfer method to prepare checksums and acceptance scripts appropriately).

I'll prepare a short automation tarball (checks and verification scripts) and place it in the same secure folder as the manifest; we will provide checksums and detached signatures for each script.

-Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

2) Sign-off template: we have a 1-page signoff PDF in the rollforward-playbook that your on-site POC can sign and return to ops_team@redwood.com. This is sufficient for our audit trail.
3) Timeboxed escalation: if rollback is initiated, Redwood on-call will be engaged immediately — please call the number in the playbook and also open the SUP-9012 ticket (link attached).

We are available to come on-site virtually at the start of the window to watch the gates run and help interpret logs. If Gravitas can confirm physical media transfer method and POC name by EOD tomorrow, we'll finalize the tarball with checksums and a separate detached signature for each helper script.

Regards,
